bullets.title: MRVL: $120B Google XPU Deal Transforms Revenue Outlook; Wolfe OW $250, KeyBanc OW $400
bullets.body: Marvell signed a commercial agreement with Google covering AI inference accelerators, storage controllers, NICs, memory interface controllers, and near-memory compute, with Google receiving 59M warrants at $206.58 (vesting in $500M revenue tranches through FY33), implying $120B+ revenue potential over ~5.5 years vs. $9B FY27 consensus. Wolfe upgrades to Outperform with $250 PT (15.7% upside from $216), calling it MRVL's 'AMD moment'; KeyBanc maintains OW at $400 (39x F29 EPS $10.31), noting MRVL is the first semi to receive Google warrants—Broadcom has not received equivalent. Stock soared 12-14% premarket.

bullets.title: AVGO: Negative Read-Through from MRVL-Google Deal; Down ~4% Premarket
bullets.body: Broadcom fell ~2.9-4% premarket as the MRVL-Google custom silicon partnership raised concerns about AVGO's share of Google's TPU ecosystem. AVGO management had previously acknowledged it is unlikely to retain all TPU share indefinitely; FY27 AI revenue forecast already debated at $116B vs. prior $100B target and investor expectations of $130B. AVGO was down 6 of 7 prior sessions amid ASIC ramp visibility concerns.

bullets.title: NVDA: Estimates Raised ~$1B/$1.5B Above Street for Jul/Oct Quarters; AI Semis Consensus $133B
bullets.body: Citi raises NVDA Jul/Oct-Q sales estimates ~$1B and $1.5B above Street respectively, citing secured HBM memory supply for 2026/27. Goldman models AI semis revenue at $133B vs. Street $118B and management guidance >$100B. NVDA, INTC, and GFS management all confirmed power-constrained environment as critical AI datacenter bottleneck.

bullets.title: TLN: Down 11% on PA Governor's Data Center Executive Order; Existing Deals Likely Grandfathered
bullets.body: Talen Energy fell 11% after Pennsylvania Governor Shapiro enacted an executive order removing data centers from fast-track permitting and barring NDA use, described as 'strictest guardrails in the nation.' Analysts believe TLN's existing deals are grandfathered, expect stock to bounce from low-end range, but flag additional pressure on EXC and PPL with more contentious projects.

bullets.title: PSP/Data Center Power: WULF Hyperscaler Deal Confirmed; AI Power Scarcity Thesis Intact
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes WULF CEO confirmed signing a hyperscaler customer deal at its 480MW Kentucky site (15-year terms, 15% FCF yields, ~$15/watt value creation). The broader PSP thesis remains intact with customers urgently requesting near-term 2027 power capacity; CIFR equity value modeled at $43.50/share at 8% financing cost, declining to $27/share at +400bps. PA and ERCOT regulatory headlines viewed as technical/event-driven, not thesis-changing.

bullets.title: SNOW: Mizuho Raises PT to $355 on AI Product Adoption; TEAM Also Constructive Near-Term
bullets.body: Mizuho raises Snowflake PT to $355 (from $295) on strong CoCo/CoWork AI product adoption and data modernization demand. Jefferies software analyst separately names TEAM and SNOW as most constructive near-term inflection picks in software, while CRM and WDAY AI monetization pushed to 2027/2028.

bullets.title: META: Down ~8% Over Two Days Amid Child Safety Trial and AI Capex Concerns
bullets.body: Meta posted back-to-back ~4% daily declines, lagging the market by 670bps over two days and is flat on a two-year basis. Headwinds include an Oakland child safety advisory jury trial (non-binding verdict), growing concerns on capital intensity and AI infrastructure lease obligations, and Oracle credit spread widening raising broader hyperscaler credit questions.

bullets.title: MSFT/AMZN/GOOGL: Jefferies Stays Buy on Hyperscalers; AMZN Down 6 Straight Sessions
bullets.body: Jefferies software analyst reiterates Buy on MSFT, AMZN, and GOOGL on hyperscaler positioning, preferring AMZN and MSFT on relative value with ROI argument intact. Goldman flags AMZN down 6 days in a row and 9 of 11, underperforming internet peers. GOOGL sold A$5.5B in Australian debt at ~7%, highest rate ever for the company.

bullets.title: MDB: GS Sees 6-7x Valuation Discount to Peers; Atlas Growth 29%+ Expected in F2Q
bullets.body: Goldman expects MongoDB Atlas growth of 29%+ in F2Q (vs 26% guidance) and mid-20s%+ in F3Q vs Street +22%, supported by npm download growth accelerating to 80%+ YoY in F2Q27 vs ~55% in F1Q27. MDB trades at a 6-7x EV/Sales discount to SNOW and DDOG on forward metrics despite the stock being up >30% in the past month.

bullets.title: NBIS: $4.5B Convertible Notes Offering to Fund GPU Procurement and AI Data Centers; Stock -4.7%
bullets.body: Nebius Group launched $4.5B in convertible senior notes ($2.75B due 2030 at 0-0.5% coupon, $1.75B due 2034 at 4-4.5% coupon) to finance data center construction, GPU cluster (H100/Blackwell) procurement, and full-stack AI cloud development. Stock fell 4.7% premarket on the dilutive offering; pricing expected post-close August 19.

bullets.title: CIEN/CRDO/LITE/FN: Optical and Networking Names Rally on MRVL Halo; Multiple Upgrades
bullets.body: CIEN gained 3.4% premarket after Northland Capital Markets upgrade; FN upgraded by Fox Advisors (+2.4%); LITE +3.3%, CRDO +2.5%, and AAOI +5.9% all benefiting from MRVL-Google AI silicon tailwind. Wolfe Research is hosting ECOC 2026 investor meetings with CIEN, COHR, CSCO, CRDO, LITE, and NOK executives Sept 21-22.

bullets.title: MU: US-Made DRAM Commands Premium; Hyperscalers Willing to Pay Up for Domestic Supply
bullets.body: Commentary notes US hyperscalers are willing to pay a premium for Micron's US-made DRAM, with domestic semiconductor manufacturing increasingly valued. MU also gained 2.4% premarket on earnings.

bullets.title: VST/CEG: 100% Binding PPA Ratios vs. NEE/BE Higher Ghost Ratios; Nuclear Re-Contracting Active
bullets.body: ESG research notes Constellation and Vistra have 100% binding ratios on PPA deals vs. NextEra (5.0x ghost ratio) and Bloom (2.6x). Morgan Stanley reports NEE re-contracted Point Beach nuclear capacity with WEC on 20-year terms starting 2030/2033 with expected savings vs. existing PPA. BE and GNRC weighted at 40%/40% in Citi's China auto index reshuffling.

bullets.title: HUT: Freedom Capital Initiates Buy at $132; Stock Down 4.1% Despite Positive Catalyst
bullets.body: Freedom Capital initiated HUT 8 Corp with a Buy rating and $132 price target, but the stock traded down 4.1% in Canadian trading, likely on broader crypto/AI infrastructure risk-off amid rate pressure and Asian tech selloff.

bullets.title: ABNB: At 52-Week High, +48.8% YTD as Breadth Favors Outperformers
bullets.body: Airbnb reached a new 52-week high at $186.80, up 1.9% on the day and +48.8% over the past 52 weeks, appearing in StreetAccount's 52-week high list with Health Technology dominating new highs (61 stocks).

bullets.title: AMZN: Drone Delivery Expanding to ~500 U.S. Cities Including Suburban Chicago and Atlanta
bullets.body: Amazon is expanding its Prime Air drone delivery service to nearly 500 U.S. cities and towns, with suburban Chicago and Atlanta announced as latest additions. The program has already delivered hundreds of thousands of packages in 2024 and is transitioning from R&D toward commercial operations.

bullets.title: DKNG: Pennsylvania iGaming +9.1%, Sports Wagering +27.8% YoY in July; Retail Slots Soft
bullets.body: Pennsylvania July gaming revenues totaled $591.1M (+6.0% YoY), with iGaming at $249.0M (+9.1% YoY) and sports wagering net revenue $51.8M (+27.8% YoY, $509.5M handle +23.5%). Retail casino slots/tables remained weak across all operators, a modest negative read for brick-and-mortar exposure but positive for DraftKings' digital-focused model.

bullets.title: INTC: Nova Lake-S 'Core Ultra 9 4950K' Naming Leak; ES Allegedly Faster Than All Current-Gen Intel CPUs
bullets.body: An alleged Intel Core Ultra 9 4950K engineering sample surfaced, pointing to a new naming scheme for Nova Lake-S desktop CPUs and reportedly outperforming all current-generation Intel offerings; directional positive for INTC competitive positioning but pre-production.

bullets.title: CRWV: Jefferies AI Summit Sept 22-23 Features CoreWeave as Participant
bullets.body: CoreWeave will participate in the Jefferies AI Summit Sept 22-23 at Lake Merced Golf Club, CA, alongside CRM and 30+ AI companies. The summit focuses on enterprise AI adoption transitioning from experimentation to deployment.
